problem_statement: The syscon register interface has two gaps. First, there is no way to atomically read-modify-write a subset of a register's bits: a caller cannot clear and set specific bit positions in a single, lock-protected operation, so concurrent accessors can race on a separate read followed by a write. Second, a register offset that is not a multiple of the register's byte width is silently rounded down to the nearest aligned offset instead of being rejected, so a caller requesting an out-of-alignment offset reads or writes the wrong register with no error reported.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_cortex_a53 -T tests/drivers/syscon -s tests/drivers/syscon/drivers.syscon -s drivers.syscon -O twister-out --no-clean -W

problems.detail: The hidden tests call syscon_update_bits(), but the statement only describes an atomic read-modify-write feature without giving the public function name or signature.

The hidden tests check specific update semantics: bits selected by mask are replaced by the corresponding bits from val, bits not selected are preserved, and a zero mask leaves the register unchanged. The statement does not specify this clearly enough.

The hidden tests expect -EINVAL for misaligned and out-of-range register offsets from syscon_read_reg(), syscon_write_reg(), and syscon_update_bits(), but the statement only says the offset is rejected without giving the exact error code.

leak_check.suggested_statement: The syscon register interface has two gaps. First, there is no way to atomically read-modify-write a subset of a register's bits: a caller cannot clear and set specific bit positions in a single, lock-protected operation, so concurrent accessors can race on a separate read followed by a write. A new function syscon_update_bits(const struct device *dev, uint16_t reg, uint32_t mask, uint32_t val) returning int must be added to the syscon driver API. It must atomically replace the bits selected by mask with the corresponding bits from val (equivalent to read the register, compute (old & ~mask) | (val & mask), and write the result) with respect to other syscon operations on the same device. If the register offset is misaligned or out of bounds, it must return -EINVAL. Second, a register offset that is not a multiple of the register's byte width must be rejected with -EINVAL instead of being silently rounded down to the nearest aligned offset, so a caller requesting an out-of-alignment offset reads or writes the wrong register with no error reported. All read, write, and update_bits operations must reject misaligned offsets with -EINVAL.
